summary.title: Claim Julian Champagnie (waivers) and drop Ace Bailey
summary.headline: Waiver claim on Julian Champagnie (SAS SF/PF; waivers clear Thu Oct 22; we hold priority 1, user-reported), dropping Ace Bailey.
summary.verdict:
Recommended: the only free move that improves P(playoffs), P(title) and category wins by > 2 SE under all three projection sets.
Costs ~1 pp of this week's P(win) (Champagnie plays 2 games from Oct 23, Bailey loses 2).
Needs your explicit yes before I place the claim; the claim must be in before waivers process on Oct 22.

metrics.label: Δ this week's P(win) vs Joshua's

risks: Cells are ΔP(playoffs) pp / ΔP(title) pp / Δcat-wins; ± are Monte Carlo SEs only (seed-aware), not model error.
Another manager may claim Champagnie; waiver priority 1 is user-reported, not verified on Yahoo.
Bailey is a 20-year-old rookie: projections for rookies are least certain (upside not captured).
Simulator is optimistic for us (opponents never manage rosters); the gain is small but consistent across projection sets.
rationale: Julian Champagnie is a 3-and-D forward (San Antonio, SF/PF): he hits threes, rebounds a bit, and rarely turns it over. Ace Bailey is a 20-year-old rookie scorer whose role and efficiency are uncertain.
Over a full season Champagnie is projected to play ~10 more games (72 vs 62) and to give us more 3-pointers and rebounds at better efficiency; Bailey gives a bit more points and assists.

The paired season simulations favour Champagnie under all three projection sets (ours, the ESPN+FantasyPros market blend, and ESPN-only): about +1.6 to +2.4 pp title odds and +0.7 to +1.1 pp playoff odds, each > 2 SE.
- Cost this week: about −1 pp of P(win vs Joshua's) — Bailey loses 2 games before Champagnie can play (claim clears Oct 22, he plays from Oct 23).

- Cost the model doesn't capture: our waiver priority goes from 1st to last (rolling list), so we'd be behind everyone for the next breakout pickup; and Bailey's rookie upside (if he wins a bigger role, his value could rise mid-season).

why_now.before: At the draft (pick 156, our last) the model had Bailey and Champagnie in an exact tie: optimizer score 5.617 vs 5.617, and the 48-rollout season simulation gave Bailey 35.18% vs 34.99% title odds — a 0.2 pp gap well inside its noise. Our rule was 'always take the top recommendation', so the tie went to Bailey.

changed.text: Much more precise evidence: 8 seeds × 2,000 paired seasons per projection set instead of 48 rollouts, so a 1.5-2 pp edge is now clearly above noise.
Robustness across projection sets (new since the draft): the market projections value Bailey far lower (0.59 vs Champagnie 0.97), our own model slightly lower (1.08 vs 1.26).

Simulator upgrades since the draft: position-aware daily lineups and IL replacement (season-sim-0.6.0); the C/PF crunch costs ~0 games, so Bailey's SF eligibility (a draft-time roster need) no longer buys anything — Champagnie is SF/PF too.
Champagnie went undrafted and is free to claim; no games have been played yet, so this is not a reaction to on-court news.
